- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% relative to model output.
- Underestimate prices during bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 2–5% to forecast to compensate for underreaction.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — if last 3–5 prices are rising sharply, cap forecast increase to avoid overshoot.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment was high 2–3 days prior, forecast should be slightly higher than baseline; if low, slightly lower.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, avoid assuming linear continuation — if sentiment is volatile, use 10–15% smoothing on trend changes.
- Don’t ignore sentiment reversal: if sentiment drops sharply within 3 days, reduce forecast slope and add downward bias of 1–3% per day.
